evidence.claim: Railways subsequently used the same advantage of the river valleys.
evidence.quote: With the arrival of trains, river valleys again provided the path of least resistance.

evidence.claim: The county seat’s courthouse was built in 1907 to a design by Smith & Carrier, with a polygonal cupola above its hipped roof.
evidence.quote: It was designed by noted Asheville architectural firm of Smith & Carrier and built in 1907.  It is two-story, brick, Classical Revival-style building.  It has a hipped roof topped by a four-stage polygonal cupola.

evidence.claim: The river setting also carries a recent history of destruction: Hurricane Helene damaged the town hall and destroyed several buildings in 2024.
evidence.quote: The town was impacted by Hurricane Helene in 2024. The hurricane destroyed several buildings in Marshall, and damaged the town hall.

evidence.claim: A Methodist meeting place became an early school in Weaverville.
evidence.quote: a large conference house (built in the 1830s) housed the Methodist assembly which became the first school in the area in 1840.

evidence.claim: The conference house, built in the 1830s on the Reems Creek Camp Grounds, took on its educational role in 1840.
evidence.quote: On land first known as the Reems Creek Camp Grounds, a large conference house (built in the 1830s) housed the Methodist assembly which became the first school in the area in 1840.

evidence.claim: Weaverville College followed with a charter in 1873, later becoming a junior college and merging with Rutherford and Brevard Colleges in 1934.
evidence.quote: A four-year college, it was downsized in 1912 to junior college status, merging in 1934 with Rutherford and Brevard Colleges to continue in Brevard.

evidence.claim: The town’s Methodist church was built in 1919–1920, with a two-story front portico and a later educational building added in 1956–1957.
evidence.quote: It was built in 1919–1920, and is a two-story, five-bay, brick church with Classical Revival and Late Gothic Revival design influences.  The front facade features a two-story, three-bay portico.  Attached to the church is the educational building constructed in 1956–1957.
